notes: Category 3 of the taxonomy in docs/pool_edge_plan.md: the interval contains both zero AND the hypothesised effect, so the test said nothing. These are NOT negatives.
The evaluator resolves ~2 ATS points (RWB-15). Most single features are worth a fraction of that, so landing here is the DEFAULT outcome for a real small signal.
Effects are stored so POSITIVE FAVOURS THE CANDIDATE regardless of the metric's own polarity; Brier and MAE must be negated before recording.
A pooled estimate justifies ONE predeclared combined look on a rotation window none of the inputs touched. It is never itself a finding.

It measures accuracy on a small, self-selected sample of 51 chosen picks rather than the whole week's card, and the limited data leaned against this ranking method.

cfb_qb_dependence_interaction.classification_evidence: Week-blocked accuracy P+=0.5140 (below 0.75 clear bar), Brier P+=0.3633 with no resolved gain (below 0.90 bar); both 95% intervals straddle zero comfortably (do not exclude zero on the wrong side, so bounded_by_control does not apply). Point estimate (+0.0224 pts) sits at ~2.05% of this screen's own MDE80 floor (1.093 pts, f=0.1385, n=9093) -- below detection power, not evidence of zero effect. Step 0 split-half reliability is 0.9588 (interaction), 0.9581/0.9923 (constituents) -- far above this repo's no-split-half-reliability examples (0.063, 0.014) and even above its own cleared precedents (0.68-0.93), ruling out refuted_mechanism.
cfb_qb_dependence_interaction.description: CFB QB-dependence interaction (raw qb_starter_epa_per_dropback x off_pass_rate, per side, differenced) vs the frozen XLG-03 CFB benchmark, candidate adds the interaction plus its two constituent diff columns alongside the baseline.
cfb_qb_dependence_interaction.notes: CFB screen only; NFL Step 3 (interaction columns using qb_starter_epa_per_dropback vs the injury-blended qb_expected_epa_per_dropback, NFL rotation-family declaration) is explicitly deferred to a separate, later, separately predeclared spec per docs/qb_dependence.md. This result does not authorize any NFL rotation window.
cfb_qb_dependence_interaction.plain_summary: College football: this tests adding a new ingredient to the prediction model -- how much value each team's starting quarterback creates per play, multiplied by how often that team throws the ball, added as an extra input alongside the model's existing stats. The underlying quarterback-value measurement itself is very consistent and repeatable from one half of the season to the other, but adding it to the model this way came back an almost exact coin flip for whether it actually improves predictions, and this result only concerns the college football version of the test -- a separate NFL version has not been run yet.

cfb_role_continuity.classification_evidence: Reclassified 2026-08-18 from closed_negative. The recorded -0.672 pts reproduces bit-for-bit, but it sits BELOW the instrument's own MDE80 of 0.927 pts (f=9.96%, n=9093), so it was never resolvable. Split-half reliability of the traits is 0.719 (dropback) and 0.680 (carry) on 1658/1671 team-seasons -- comparable to injury_value_lost's kept 0.87-0.93 and far above the 0.063/0.014 reliabilities that correctly closed other lines -- which rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability'. No positive control bounds this family (the +0.0129 MAE deliberate-leak control belongs to opponent adjustment, a different family, and was not borrowed). Neither admissible closing ground is met. A family-specific refit-aware bootstrap (measured inflation 1.438x, inside the documented 17-58% band) gives -0.078 pts P+ 0.367, converging with the sign-only read of -0.101.
cfb_role_continuity.description: CFB dropback/carry participation-continuity family (season-scoped, streak-capped) vs the frozen XLG-03 arm.
cfb_role_continuity.notes: This closure was gating the XLG-04 -> XLG-05 cross-league transfer path; that path should be treated as open again. Reopening XLG-05 itself is a separate decision. Sign still leans negative.
cfb_role_continuity.plain_summary: College football: this tests whether tracking how consistently the same players have been getting the ball (handoffs and pass targets) game to game, capped so a long streak doesn't dominate, adds anything to the prediction model beyond what it already uses. The underlying continuity measurement itself repeats reasonably well from one half of the season to the other, but adding it to the model leaned slightly toward hurting accuracy rather than helping, and this result reopens a related question about whether a similar idea could work across a different sport-to-sport comparison.

cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gate_direct.classification_evidence: Cleanest evidence the gating recipe produces: gating improved on the ungated candidate directly at P+ 0.881, even though the resulting gated arm is still net-negative against the true baseline (see cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gated_vs_baseline). Interval still crosses zero at the lower bound.
cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gate_direct.description: Direct paired comparison of the disagreement-gated cfb_role_continuity candidate against its own ungated form (same real outcomes) -- tests whether gating itself helps, not whether the candidate beats the true baseline.
cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gate_direct.notes: DETECTION-METHOD finding about the gating recipe, not a new predictive feature -- same status as the already-registered estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_full_vs_thin_cfb. DO-NOT-POOL: correlated with cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gated_vs_baseline (same gate, same 8,933 games).
cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gate_direct.plain_summary: College football: not a bet on any game situation: this checks a technical question about how to build the previous participation-continuity feature -- specifically, whether only trusting it in games where the model's inputs already disagree with each other (a filtering technique) does better than using the feature everywhere without that filter. The limited data leaned toward the filtering technique helping, but this only says something about how to build that one feature, not whether the underlying idea beats the model's true baseline.

cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gated_vs_ba.classification_evidence: Gating more than doubled P+ (0.026 -> 0.063) and cut the loss roughly in half vs the already-registered cfb_role_continuity's ungated -0.67 pts, but did not resolve the comparison or flip its sign against the true baseline.
cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gated_vs_ba.description: cfb_role_continuity, gated by a conditional-median threshold on absent_mass (0.6614, derived from the distribution, not from accuracy) vs the TRUE baseline (market_residual).
cfb_role_continuity_surgical_gated_vs_ba.notes: sample_blocks=351 is the RETAINED-DISAGREEMENT count (351 of 890 total disagreements), NOT a week-block count -- UNCONFIRMED as a true week-block figure, verify before recording. reliability=0.70 inherited/rounded from cfb_role_continuity's own trait reliabilities (0.719 dropback / 0.680 carry) since this is the same underlying trait, gated -- not independently re-measured for the gated form. cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.classification_evidence: Week-blocked accuracy interval [-0.402,+0.208]pts crosses zero (P+=0.2491); season-blocked agrees ([-0.390,+0.227]pts, P+=0.2537). Neither meets a closing ground: no resolved wrong sign (interval not entirely negative) and split-half reliability of the new value-weighted trait is confidently POSITIVE not indistinguishable from zero (dropback SB=0.033 P+=0.958, carry SB=0.049 P+=0.986; averaged to 0.041 for this field) -- far below the plain cfb_role_continuity trait's own 0.719/0.680, so the refuted_mechanism reliability route is also unavailable. Brier (P+=0.098) and log-loss (P+=0.027) lean the same negative direction as a coherence check only, never overriding. Standalone arm, not stacked with plain continuity, per adjudicated decision 3.
cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.description: Value-weighted (credited-play-EPA-rate x usage-share) CFB dropback/carry role continuity, standalone arm, vs the frozen XLG-03 cfb_benchmark_v1 arm.
cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.notes: Predeclared only as a scratchpad DRAFT (rapm_scope/predeclaration_draft.md + implementation_plan.md), never frozen into docs/; reframed from RAPM (not buildable on CFB's credited-actor-only data) to value-weighted role continuity. VALUE_RELIABILITY_PRIOR_PLAYS=500 / VALUE_EPA_CLIP=5.0 mirrored verbatim from NFL participation.py -- EXPLICITLY UNDERIVED for CFB's play volume/EPA distribution (adjudicated decision 5). Weight formula 'state x value_rate' is an inferred reading of an ambiguity the adjudication did not resolve (see results.md deviation 2). Mechanically flagged: ~50.7% of team-game rows fall back to neutral via active_mass sign-cancellation (45.1% of qualifying player-games have negative value_rate), and the non-neutral continuity tail is unbounded (dropback [-286.9,+233.7], carry [-40.3,+343.2]) -- a likely instrument-design defect in the literal weight formula, not just a power limit; a rectified weight was not tried (would be a new, undeclared family). Source: scripts/cfb_value_weighted_continuity_screen.py, artifacts/cfb_value_weighted_continuity/20260818T211758Z/. Reviewer note 2026-08-18: the actionable finding is the instrument defect, not the effect -- the state-times-value_rate weight cancels ~50.7% of team-game rows to neutral via sign cancellation and has unbounded tails (dropback [-287, +234]); split-half reliability 0.033-0.049 is confidently positive but ~5-15% of the plain trait's 0.68-0.72. Any successor should redesign the weight (e.g. magnitude-based) before re-screening; this entry prices the tested formula only.
cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.plain_summary: College football: tests whether valuing which players return at each roster spot by how many effective plays they're worth, not just whether the same player returns, predicts covering the spread better than the model's existing player-continuity measure. The limited data leaned against it, but more importantly, the person who reviewed this found the way 'value' was calculated has a design flaw -- about half of all team-games get treated as neutral by an accident of the math -- so this specific result describes a flawed measuring instrument, not a settled answer about whether the underlying idea works.

combined_stacker_opener_2022_2023.classification_evidence: Predeclared single look (docs/combined_stacker_predeclaration.md, frozen 2026-08-21). Paired delta candidate-minus-baseline at the opener: -0.973 accuracy points over 514 games / 36 week blocks; week-blocked 95% [-2.9015, +0.9452], probability_positive 0.13325. The primary interval does not sit wholly below zero and no positive control was run, so neither admissible terminal classification applies per AGENTS.md; below the 0.90 claim gate, hence unresolved_below_power. Season-blocked secondary [-1.50, -0.40] (two blocks, degenerate by construction) leans negative but never gates. Brier/log-loss direction-only secondaries favour the candidate weakly (P+ 0.547/0.551 week-blocked): the added columns carry slight probabilistic information that did not convert into better forced picks on this window.
combined_stacker_opener_2022_2023.description: Combined four-column stacker (injury-value-lost narrowed top-tertile pair + kn temp-gap-cold-visitor pre2020 + warm-team-cold-late pre2020 + spread-gap zone) on the production weak_stack recipe, paired opener-grade confirmation look on [2022, 2023], production probability rule.
combined_stacker_opener_2022_2023.notes: Candidate arm = weak_stack profile plus 4 appended columns (90->94), ridge alpha 10, walk-forward min_train_games 500, training strictly prior; both arms graded by clv.opener_pick_evaluation restricted to rotation window via confirmation_split; bootstrap 20000 samples seed 20260817. Baseline self-check: appending columns leaves baseline picks bit-identical. Leakage conventions: tercile boundaries strictly-prior completed REG games only; climate_temp from strictly-earlier outdoor home games (pregame-safe adaptation documented in forecast_cold_visitor_tilt_overlay); missing inputs fail closed. Window carries the acknowledged mined-ledger discount; no input family had touched 2022-2023 before this look. DO-NOT-POOL with mod07_opener_bias_ablation / injury_value_lost family reads: different windows and populations; shares the mod07 lineage only through the baseline recipe. Column flag prevalence in window: ivl_home 191, ivl_away 197, kn_temp_gap 32, warm_cold_late 6, spread_gap_zone 62 of 514.
combined_stacker_opener_2022_2023.plain_summary: This tests bolting four separate situational betting angles -- an injury-value matchup rule, a pre-2020 cold-weather-visitor angle, a pre-2020 warm-team-in-cold-weather angle, and a betting-line-size zone -- onto the model's production recipe all at once, checked against the plain production recipe alone at the actual Tuesday opening line, on a 2022-2023 slice of games set aside for this kind of confirmation check. The limited data leaned against the combined version, and the sample and the four extra factors overlap with other results recorded separately, so this shouldn't be read as a fresh, independent test of any one of them.

era_trend_hc_year_one_fade.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- betting against a team playing under a first-season head coach during weeks 1 through 8 -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. Unlike most of these era-drift checks, this one shows a real, statistically clear upward trend: the edge has been getting stronger over time, essentially appearing out of nothing before around 2018-2019 and growing large since, roughly tracking how many first-year head coaches are around the league in a given season; this pattern is used elsewhere in the project as a known, already-established benchmark case.

estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.classification_evidence: Own-model pick stability: single-fit pairwise flip rate (two individual bootstrap-refit draws disagreeing) 26.4% vs bagged split-half flip rate (mean of first 60 vs mean of second 60 of 120 refit draws disagreeing) 4.5% -- a 5.9x reduction, on 8,933 CFB games / 13 seasons. Accuracy: single-fit 51.14% vs bagged 51.31% (+0.17 pts, bagging beats the single fit). Bagged-vs-baseline (full-vs-thin) paired comparison: -0.168 acc pts [naive interval], P+ 0.383 (up from the single-fit arm's -0.336 pts / P+ 0.262 -- still crosses zero, so unresolved, but a genuine partial improvement in both estimate and P+ relative to not bagging). A DIRECT synthetic falsification attempt (fresh-bootstrap-of-a-training-resample own-model-instability design) found a null result instead (single flip 9.5% vs bagged 10.0%); diagnosed as a comparator design flaw (bootstrapping a bootstrap resample compounds variance rather than testing a fair 'fresh draw of history'), not evidence against the real-data finding. The real-data split-half design (splitting one clean bootstrap ensemble in half, no nested resampling) is the trustworthy comparator.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.description: Average predicted centres over training-row bootstrap-refit draws (bagging) instead of reporting a single point-estimate fit. Screened on the CFB thin-vs-full candidate comparison, reusing the refit draws already computed for the honest interval -- no extra fitting.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.notes: The flip-rate reduction (pick stability) is the strong, decisive part of this result; the accuracy/P+ improvement is real but modest and does not clear any promotion bar on its own. Recommend bagging as a default variance-reduction step for FUTURE candidate screens (it cannot move any current pick since it is not wired into any production path), not as a standalone accuracy claim. P+ 0.383'); +0.17 was actually the SEPARATE bagged-vs-single-fit accuracy delta (51.31% vs 51.14%), not the bagged-vs-baseline comparison this P+ describes. Recorded here as effect=-0.168 to match docs/estimation_variance.md sec 4a's literal 'Bagged vs. baseline, naive interval | -0.17 pts [naive], P+ 0.383' under this registry's positive-favours-candidate convention. The underlying finding (bagging helps, relative to the single fit) is unchanged by this correction; only the sign of the recorded full-vs-thin effect number is fixed.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.plain_summary: College football: tests averaging many slightly different refits of the model together, each trained on a random resample of the same games, rather than trusting a single fit -- a technique aimed at making the model's picks more stable from one run to the next, not necessarily at finding a bigger edge. The clearest result was that this noticeably cut down how often the model's pick for a game flipped between runs; the effect on picking accuracy itself was real but modest and doesn't by itself meet the bar for switching to this approach live, so it's recommended as good practice for testing future ideas rather than a change affecting any pick made today.

estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.classification_evidence: Non-monotonic and noisy: shrink_fraction=1.0 (production strength) gives -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.255; 0.75 -> -0.448 pts P+ 0.181; 0.5 -> -0.414 pts P+ 0.208; 0.25 -> +0.034 pts P+ 0.543 (essentially zero, not a real flip, just the least-negative point); 0.0 -> -1.209 pts P+ 0.041. A matched synthetic check (linear DGP, location-biased residual sample, 100 replicates x n_boot=50) found the OPPOSITE, clean, monotonic pattern instead: shrink=1.0 always best (+1.67 pts, P+ 0.707), declining smoothly to shrink=0 (-5.52 pts, P+ 0.091). Flip-rate DOES fall monotonically with shrinkage in both the real and synthetic data (confirms the mechanism -- production's cover probability threshold is fixed against a nonzero-location residual sample, so uniform positive scaling is NOT sign-invariant, unlike coefficient scaling closed by MOD-06), but the real-data accuracy/P+ sweep does not replicate the synthetic monotonic decline, so there is no basis to claim a shrinkage sweet spot exists.
estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.description: Uniformly shrinking the predicted market-residual CENTRE (not the residual-sample READER, which residual_location.md already found inert) toward the market line by a fraction before reading the out-of-time residual ECDF. estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.notes: Do not treat shrink=0.25's near-zero, barely-positive point estimate as a discovery -- it is the least-bad of five noisy negative-leaning arms, not a validated improvement. The sign flip and P+ jump REPLICATE independently on two disjoint season halves built by alternating clean-core seasons (scripts/estvar_f_lever_splithalf.py): half A (2012/14/16/18/21/23/25) P+ 0.399 -> 0.935 at tau 0->0.05; half B (2013/15/17/19/22/24) P+ 0.241 -> 0.744 at tau 0->0.05. estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.description: Gate the 'full' CFB feature profile's influence to games where its predicted cover probability disagrees with the 'thin' (market+context+experience only) baseline by at least tau, deferring to the baseline elsewhere. Tests the general 'f lever' principle (MDE80 = 280*sqrt(f/n)): a surgical candidate that only moves the picks it has real information about is more provable than one that perturbs every pick.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.notes: This is a DETECTION-METHOD finding, not a new predictive feature -- 'full' and 'thin' are both already-existing profiles. The actionable implication is a general design principle for evaluating future candidates (gate influence to where the candidate disagrees with a simpler baseline), not a pick change. Do not promote or apply to any live model; this only screens the evaluator's own sensitivity. Recorded 2026-08-18 by a recording agent from docs/estimation_variance.md sec 5/sec 6 (the drafting session was barred from writing registry/*.json; this session verified the doc's tau=0.05 row and split-half table before recording, no fields required derivation).
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.plain_summary: College football: not a new betting angle -- this tests a general design principle for building future prediction features, checking whether a model does better by only acting on picks where it clearly disagrees with a simpler baseline model, deferring to that baseline otherwise, rather than letting every feature influence every pick. The idea tested well, leaning strongly positive, but it's explicitly a lesson about how to evaluate future model changes, not a new feature to add or a pick to play.

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.classification_evidence: Out-of-screen population (thin_2006_2011 minus 2006-2007, which fall below the 500-game training floor entirely under annual-refit cadence, + regime_2020): 2,533 games, 72 blocks. Real gate (tau=0.05, frozen, not re-swept): -0.316 acc pts, honest 95% interval [-1.323, +0.699] (refit_aware_interval, samples=20000), honest P+ 0.2733 -- crosses zero, does NOT directionally replicate clean-core's positive lean (P+ 0.9505 pooled, 0.935/0.744 split-half). Required placebo control (random gate, same n=411 membership count, seed 20260818): -0.553 acc pts, P+ 0.0512 -- worse than the real gate, which is evidence the disagreement selection is not arbitrary even though neither arm beats baseline here. Gate-membership reliability (120 paired refit draws): 23.09% overall flip rate under training-row resampling (1 - flip rate = 0.7691 recorded as reliability, converted to the registry's higher-is-better convention), 32.82% among point-fit in-gate games, 21.20% among out-gate games -- real instability, not enough alone to close as no_split_half_reliability. Realized f (7.03%) and membership rate (16.23%) are far above clean-core's ~2%, consistent with the flagged sparser-market regime confound (2a caveat 2) and not separable from it in this design. MDE80 at realized f/n is 1.47 pts, worse than the design's own 0.69-pt a-priori estimate and ~6x the original screen's +0.246-pt effect -- underpowered as expected, and the honest read is directional, not resolving, and leans negative rather than positive.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.description: Out-of-screen retrospective confirmation of the tau=0.05 f-lever disagreement gate (gate the CFB full profile's influence to games where it disagrees with the thin profile by >=0.05, deferring to thin elsewhere), frozen before this run per flever_scope/design.md. Tested against a required size-matched random-gate placebo control.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.notes: Confirmation run per flever_scope/design.md (2026-08-18), orchestrator adjudication: CFB-only (no NFL window drawn), no P+ bar applied to this methodology question, placebo arm required and run. Does NOT resolve or refute the disagreement-gate mechanism; the honest single-population read here is more cautionary than the design's hoped-for outcome (directional replication) -- point estimate and P+ both lean the WRONG way relative to clean-core on this specific out-of-screen population, though not to a resolved degree. The real-vs-placebo gap is the one piece of this run that leans toward the mechanism being non-arbitrary. Do not promote or apply to any live model.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.plain_summary: College football: a planned follow-up confirmation, on a fresh set of games not used in the original test, of the design idea that a model should only override a simpler baseline on picks where it clearly disagrees with that baseline -- tested here against a required 'do-nothing' comparison that applies the same kind of override at random. On this new set of games the result actually leaned the wrong way and did not repeat the earlier promising result, though not cleanly enough to call the idea disproven; the fact that it still beat the random-override comparison is the one piece of this check that still points toward the idea being real rather than arbitrary.

graph_schedule_rating_brier.plain_summary: This tests adding team-strength ratings computed the same way search engines rank web pages -- treating each week's schedule as a network of who-beat-whom and finding the most influential teams in it -- as extra ingredients in the model's market-comparison features. It's measured on how well the model's stated probabilities matched reality (a calibration score, not the usual pick-accuracy percentage), and no supporting data file survives from when this was originally run, only a written note; the limited data leaned away from the idea.

groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.classification_evidence: Interval contains zero. Recorded rather than discarded per the three-kinds-of-negative rule. THREE caveats that must travel with it: (a) this is the MAX over 22 configurations, so its sign is NOT one clean bit under the null and it must be excluded from any pooled sign test; (b) the accuracy dose-response is non-monotone; (c) the picks it relocates are won at only 50.8% (1,116 of 2,195). The Brier half IS resolved and monotone across the predeclared symmetric grid (market_light_10 +0.000304 [+0.000055, +0.000589], P+ 0.9915), with the block allocation, not the global alpha, as the resolvable half.
groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.description: Per-feature-block ridge penalties (light on market columns, heavy on thin player columns) rather than one global alpha. CFB screen, 11,989 games.
groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.notes: Blocked behind deriving ridge_alpha: at the production alpha=10 the entire block axis is a no-op (median principal direction shrunk 0.27%). Route the Brier gain to the Best Pick ranker, where Brier is the right currency.
groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.plain_summary: College football: this tests applying a different amount of statistical smoothing to different groups of the model's input columns -- lighter smoothing on well-established betting-market numbers, heavier smoothing on thinner player-level stats -- instead of one single smoothing setting for everything. At the smoothing level the model actually uses in production this change makes almost no difference either way, so it was shelved rather than adopted, even though the limited data leaned toward it helping.

hc_year_one_fade.classification_evidence: Era split is the whole question: clean 2009-2017 gap is +0.09 (n=391), mined 2018-2025 gap is -8.08 (n=465). The clean era REFUTES the -8 magnitude but NOT a moderate true effect -- a true -4 sits only 1.43 sigma from the clean-era observation, so it is not excluded. An earlier draft of this session called that a category-2 close; that was wrong and is corrected here. Escapes the closed coach-quality-reputation mechanism (reliability 0.063), which is a claim about a persistent coach TRAIT; this is an event/transition claim needing no stable trait. Not the team-quality ceiling either: invariant to quality by construction, and the gap survives inside the low-quality tercile (45.75% vs 51.46%).
hc_year_one_fade.description: First-year head coaches, weeks 1-8, cover below the kept-coach rate. Reproduced by two independent pipelines: 46.73% year-one vs 50.99% kept-coach on 856 games, gap -4.26 points.
hc_year_one_fade.notes: SCALE: the raw effect is a 4.26-point cover-rate gap on the 783 games (17.7% of the slate) with a first-year coach in weeks 1-8. Recorded on the FULL-SLATE scale so it is commensurable with feature-level accuracy deltas; an un-scaled subset effect would dominate any pool it entered. SIGN: the raw gap is negative (year-one coaches cover less); recorded positive because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the candidate HYPOTHESIS, which was exactly that they underperform. SIGN ORIENTATION: the raw cover-rate gap is -4.26 (year-one coaches cover LESS). Recorded as +4.26 because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the CANDIDATE HYPOTHESIS, and the hypothesis was exactly that they underperform -- the edge is exploitable by fading them. injury_value_lost_gradient.classification_evidence: Unchanged headline: the disagreement statistic resolves (rank-biserial +0.248 [+0.046,+0.450], p=0.016) but the ACCURACY effect does not (+1.75 [-0.69,+4.27], P+ 0.899) on the already-spent [2020, 2021] window, 456 games. NEW this session (docs/injury_value_lost.md): (1) split-half reliability of the underlying value-lost signal, measured on the full 2009-2025 history (4,431 games, 384 team-seasons, temporal odd/even-week split) is Pearson r=0.874 [0.843,0.901], Spearman-Brown corrected full-length reliability=0.933 [0.915,0.948], P+=1.000 (4000/4000 bootstrap draws) -- rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability' per AGENTS.md. (2) The RAPM-participation value-lost construct (M6, the family's one same-kind negative, -0.43 pts) has EQUALLY high reliability (0.860 raw / 0.925 corrected) -- so reliability does NOT explain M6's negative sign; more likely M6 tests the marginal value of a second, QB-inclusive, correlated value-lost construct stacked on top of one already in the model (full_player_participation = full_player_value + participation family), not whether value-lost as a concept works. (3) The mechanism-screen result survives a market-line-movement control unchanged (value_magnitude vs |close-open| line move: Pearson 0.029, near-zero; residualized disagreement rank-biserial 0.249 [0.047,0.451] p=0.016, statistically identical to the raw 0.248). (4) Survives dropping every QB-involved game: on the 397/456 games (87%) where neither presumed starter carried any listed injury, rank-biserial is still positive (+0.188 [-0.027,0.403], p=0.086) at comparable magnitude to the full sample -- consistent with the structural code finding that injury_skill_epa_value_lost deliberately zeroes QB rushing/receiving production (players.py:1260-1283), so this is provably not a QB proxy. (5) A methodologically CLEANER isolation exists and was run for the first time: player_value profile on game_features_player_value.parquet (built with FIXED-prior severity per its manifest player_feature_version=v2 tag, confirmed NOT learned) contrasted against the player baseline differs by ONLY the two value-lost columns -- zero semantics-shift confound, unlike this entry's original B-A contrast which mixed learned-severity semantics_shift into the same delta. That clean contrast gives +1.316 pts [-0.460,+3.247], P+ 0.8875, on the same 456 games, 26 disagreements (61.5% candidate win rate) -- smaller than +1.75 (removing the confound costs about a third of a point) but directionally intact. Recommend citing +1.316/P+0.8875 as the number to predeclare a narrowed family against, not the conflated +1.75 recorded here.
injury_value_lost_gradient.description: The availability/player-value half of the MOD-07 stack, whose gain concentrates in games with more injury VALUE lost rather than more availability-RATE shift. Tercile accuracy by value lost is monotone: -0.66 / +0.66 / +5.26 points.
injury_value_lost_gradient.notes: The narrowed candidate worth building: value-weighted injury magnitude with the learned-rate half dropped -- confirmed in docs/injury_value_lost.md section 4 using game_features_player_value.parquet (fixed severity) rather than the weak_stack table (learned severity), which removes the semantics-shift confound entirely. Predeclare as a new family `injury_value_lost_narrowed` inheriting mod07_weak_signal_stack (contaminates [2020,2021]); earliest eligible block after inherited contamination is [2022, 2023], one of only two remaining full opener blocks in the 2020-2025 pool. Do not assign until the 2026 prospective mod07_weak_signal_stack challenger (already ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE, artifacts/prospective/challengers.json) has produced its own number -- docs/injury_value_lost.md section 7 has the full predeclaration text to freeze verbatim. CFB cannot screen this family: value_lost requires a pregame injury-severity signal and none exists in any CFB source (docs/cfb_data.md, 'Availability semantics (fail closed)'); the nearest feasible CFB proxy (realized participation continuity, a different, postgame construct) already ran and lost (-0.67 pts on 8,933 games, cfb_role_continuity family, closed_negative).
injury_value_lost_gradient.plain_summary: Splitting games into three equal groups by how much total player value was lost to injury (weighing not just how many players were out but how important they were), games in the top third for value lost covered notably more than games in the bottom third: -0.66 points below baseline in the lowest-loss third, +0.66 in the middle third, and +5.26 in the highest-loss third. This isolates which games actually drive the edge in an injury-value feature already built into the live model.

injury_value_lost_narrowed.classification_evidence: Removes the semantics-shift half of injury_value_lost_gradient, which the mechanism screen (docs/availability_confirmation.md sec 3) showed does not itself carry the disagreement signal (semantics_shift rank-biserial -0.024, p=0.816). This is the number the project's own docs recommend predeclaring against.
injury_value_lost_narrowed.description: Value-weighted injury-lost magnitude only, with the learned-availability-rate/semantics-shift confound removed (game_features_player_value.parquet, fixed-prior severity). Confound-free re-isolation of injury_value_lost_gradient.
injury_value_lost_narrowed.notes: reliability=0.87 is COPIED from injury_value_lost_gradient's registered value (lower bound of its 0.87-0.93 range), not independently re-measured for this narrower construct -- UNCONFIRMED, flag for re-verification. DO-NOT-POOL: shares all 456 games with injury_value_lost_gradient, mod07_opener_bias_ablation, and participation_offense_defense_rapm's window family -- decomposition of the same window, not independent evidence.
injury_value_lost_narrowed.plain_summary: A cleaner version of a total-injury-value-lost measure, built to strip out a separate modeling choice (how quickly a player's injury-report status is assumed to translate into missed snaps) so what's left measures only how much player value was actually lost to injury. Tested against the model's existing setup on a shared 456-game sample also used by several closely related injury checks, so it isn't independent evidence on its own; the limited data leaned toward the idea helping accuracy.
injury_value_lost_narrowed.source: docs/injury_value_lost.md sec 4 (D-A contrast); docs/surgical_injury.md sec 2.1 (byte-exact reproduction); registry/weak_signals.json injury_value_lost_gradient.notes

injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence.classification_evidence: Interval [-1.762, +1.319] crosses zero -- not a resolved wrong sign (upper bound is positive). No positive-control bound was run. Point estimate is negative and P+ (0.3347) is below 0.5, but per AGENTS.md an interval crossing zero is never grounds to close the line at this evaluator's resolution; stays unresolved_below_power.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence.description: D-A contrast rebuilt with a synthetic injuries table keyed at the current week but built only from last week's active-roster (ACT/INA) players who recorded zero snaps in that prior game, severity fixed at 1.0 (Out-equivalent), report-independent. Tests whether a one-week-lagged, fully Tuesday-visible actual-absence signal carries value-lost information.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence.notes: Free re-read of the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] window; same 456 games, same D-A methodology as injury_value_lost_narrowed. Broader, report-independent population than injury_value_lost_prior_week_report (130,747 synthetic rows after schedule mapping vs 34,494) -- also catches non-injury roster-decision absences (healthy scratches, suspensions), a deliberate declared difference. Picks-disagreeing count differs from the report arm (17 vs 23), confirming the two arms are genuinely distinct model fits, not a duplicated construction, despite landing on the same aggregate accuracy by coincidence at n=456. Reliability of the underlying value-lost trait (0.87-0.93) was established on injury_value_lost_gradient's same-week construction, NOT independently re-measured for this construction -- left null here. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_official, injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_augmented, injury_value_lost_prior_week_report, mod07_opener_bias_ablation. Companion arm: injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence_saturday_channel (paired channel-delta). Known scope limit (predeclared): one week of lag only, does not re-derive multi-week IR persistence beyond the first lagged week.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence.plain_summary: Instead of using this week's injury report (not fully visible until later in the week), this builds an injury-value estimate purely from which key players simply didn't play any snaps in their team's game the week before -- information that is fully available by the Tuesday deadline a forced-pick pool actually uses. Tested on a shared 456-game sample also used by several related injury checks, so it isn't independent evidence on its own; the limited data leaned slightly away from this Tuesday-safe substitute carrying real value.

injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence_sat.classification_evidence: Interval [-0.871, +3.863] crosses zero -- not a resolved wrong sign. No positive-control bound was run. injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence_sat.description: Paired channel-delta, same 456 games: fresh Saturday-cutoff (real, current-week injuries) D-A minus injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence D-A. Isolates how much of the Saturday-cutoff edge a fully Tuesday-visible, one-week-lagged actual-absence substitute recovers.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence_sat.notes: Diagnostic companion to injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence, same technique injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_channel_pft_augmented used for the Tuesday+PFT arm. Tighter interval and higher P+ than the report-arm's channel-delta (injury_value_lost_prior_week_report_saturday_channel, P+ 0.8228), consistent with the absence arm's own D-A interval also being tighter. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with the full injury_value_lost family (see injury_value_lost_prior_week_report's notes for the full list).
injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence_sat.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this measures the gap between what an injury-value signal could earn using each week's real injury information as of Saturday, close to kickoff, versus what it earns using only a Tuesday-visible substitute built from the previous week's missed snaps. On a shared 456-game sample also used by several related injury checks, the limited data leaned toward a substantial gap existing, meaning much of the edge depends on late information.

injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_officia.description: injury_value_lost_narrowed D-A contrast (player_value minus player profile, game_features_player_value.parquet construction) rebuilt with a true own-week Tuesday-noon-ET decision cutoff instead of decision_hours_before_kickoff=24 (Saturday), using ONLY the official injury report's own date_modified (no PFT augmentation). Free re-read on the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] opener window, scripts/injury_tuesday_cutoff_experiment.py.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_officia.notes: Only 328/76784 (0.43%) of official injury-report rows have date_modified at or before their own game's Tuesday-noon-ET cutoff (coverage.official_rows_visible_by_tuesday_noon in the result artifact) -- the official report is structurally the wrong instrument for a Tuesday lock (NFL's first weekly practice report files Wednesday). DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, mod07_opener_bias_ablation. Companion arm: injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_augmented. Reliability of the underlying value-lost trait (0.87-0.93) was established on injury_value_lost_gradient, not independently re-measured for this Tuesday-cutoff construction.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_officia.plain_summary: This rebuilds the injury-value signal using only the league's own official injury report, checking what it would look like if a pick had to lock in at Tuesday noon rather than closer to kickoff. In practice, fewer than half a percent of the official report's entries are actually updated that early, so this version is close to using no injury information at all, and the limited data came back close to even. Tested on a shared 456-game sample also used by several related injury checks, so it isn't independent evidence on its own.

injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.classification_evidence: Point estimate is negative but the interval [-1.129, +0.668] crosses zero -- not a resolved wrong sign (requires the WHOLE interval below zero). No positive-control bound was run at this cutoff. Stays unresolved_below_power; the negative point estimate is reported, not treated as a rejection.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.description: injury_value_lost_narrowed D-A contrast rebuilt with a true own-week Tuesday-noon-ET decision cutoff, injuries table augmented: a designation is treated as visible if either its own date_modified is at/before Tuesday noon OR a ProFootballTalk injury-relevant headline (299,739-URL archive, data/raw/injury_news) names that player, dated at/before that same Tuesday noon (conservative full-name substring match, precision-favoring). Free re-read on the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] opener window.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.notes: PFT augmentation raises visible-row share from 0.43% (official-only) to 8.13% (coverage.pft_augmented_rows_visible_share, 5918 additional rows), still leaving 91.9% of designations unseen by Tuesday noon. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, mod07_opener_bias_ablation, and injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_official. Matching is a lower bound (undercounts last-name-only headlines), so this is the more-informed of the two Tuesday arms but still conservative toward finding pre-Tuesday visibility.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.plain_summary: This rebuilds the injury-value signal for a Tuesday-noon pick deadline, supplementing the league's slow-to-update official report with football-news coverage from a sports media outlet, which roughly triples how many injury updates are actually visible in time -- though it still misses the large majority of the week's designations. movement_direction_tilt_opener.classification_evidence: Interval contains zero at both week- and season-blocking (week-blocked upper bound +0.85 accuracy points, positive), so the whole interval is not on the negative side; wrong_sign_resolved does not apply. Point estimate leans negative (P+ 0.27 week-blocked, 0.23 season-blocked) but that is a lean, not a resolution. No positive-control test was run. Per AGENTS.md taxonomy this is unresolved_below_power.
movement_direction_tilt_opener.description: MOV-01 movement-direction forced-pick tilt, PRIMARY rule: flip the active weak_stack models opener pick to the movement-predicted side only when it disagrees AND predicted-move confidence is in the top half (median-split threshold computed from training-fold in-sample predictions only, never target-season data). Leak-free walk-forward reusing nfl_ats.clv.build_pilot_frame/fit_pilot_model/FROZEN_PILOT_FEATURES with no reimplementation of the model itself: seasons 2021-2023 each get a fresh expanding-window ridge refit trained only on strictly-earlier archived seasons (2021 trained on 2020 only; 2022 trained on 2020-2021; 2023 trained on 2020-2022); seasons 2024 and 2025 reuse the frozen MKT-06 pilot model AS-IS, trained once on 2020-2023 (FROZEN_PILOT_PROTOCOL), with no refit on either target season. Season 2020 excluded: no earlier archived season exists to train a leak-free direction model on. Effect and interval recorded here are OPENER-graded (project primary goal), week-blocked (90 week blocks, primary blocking). Joined population 1310 REG games, 2021-2025, against the active weak_stack opener-evaluation artifact; 59 of 276 opener-pick disagreements passed the confidence gate and were flipped.
movement_direction_tilt_opener.notes: Close-graded secondary read (same opener-anchored decision, settled at the close line via pick_correct(pick_home_at_open, margin_vs_close) -- deliberately NOT the active models own independently re-evaluated close arm, to keep the comparison apples-to-apples): delta -0.23 accuracy points, P+ 0.33 week-blocked / 0.30 season-blocked. Season-blocked bootstrap here uses only 5 blocks (2021-2025 seasons) -- thin, below the ~10-block reliability floor used elsewhere in this repo; read the week-blocked number as authoritative. Companion variants recorded separately: movement_direction_tilt_opener_variant1_no_filter (flip every disagreement) and movement_direction_tilt_opener_variant2_top_quartile (75th-percentile confidence gate).
movement_direction_tilt_opener.plain_summary: This tests overriding the model's own pick with a separate forecast of which way the betting line itself is about to move, but only when that movement forecast disagrees with the main model's pick and is relatively confident about the direction, built using only information genuinely available before each game. Tested against not overriding at all, the limited data leaned against this override helping, measured at the opening line the project treats as its main test.

offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.classification_evidence: Week-blocked clean_core interval is entirely below zero (upper -0.199 pts, P+ 0.0037); season-blocked confirms (upper -0.168, P+ 0.0066); the all-seasons superset is tighter still (upper -0.235, P+ 0.0016). Robust to the documented refit-variance correction for feature-construction families (1.003-1.099x, docs/estimation_variance.md Part II): a 10% interval widening leaves clean_core/week entirely below zero. Replicates and sharpens the existing scalar-grid CFB screen (docs/offseason_retention.md): every one of the 8 estimated per-metric values (0.166-0.350) falls inside the range that screen already showed loses to 0.67. Brier/log-loss lean the same direction but do not resolve (P+ 0.032-0.076). thin_2006_2011 and regime_2020 lean the same direction, unresolved, as expected from their lower power.
offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.description: Per-metric offseason_retention vector (CFB Route-1 season-transition slopes, horizon 4 games, values 0.166-0.350, none clipped) vs the shipped uniform 0.67 scalar, on the frozen XLG-03 CFB benchmark.
offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.notes: Scope: this refutes THIS candidate construction (CFB Route-1 horizon-4 estimate, clipped [0,1]) at the accuracy metric on the CFB instrument, not per-metric retention as a concept on other instruments. Disclosed caveat: estimation and scoring share the same 2006-2025 CFB corpus; that biases TOWARD the candidate (overfit favours it), so it strengthens rather than weakens this negative. Reviewer adjudication 2026-08-18: terminal verdict accepted -- reopening would require >36% interval widening (upper bound -0.199, centre -0.7475) against the applicable 1.003-1.099x feature-construction correction; the residual_location walk-backs used the reader-family correction, which does not apply to this fit-changing family. Actionable reading: the accuracy-optimal retention on CFB sits at or above 0.67 even though transition slopes measure 0.17-0.35 -- the state features do better carrying MORE prior-season signal than the persistence slopes suggest. DEFAULT_OFFSEASON_RETENTION=0.67 survives its audit.
offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.plain_summary: College football: this tests whether letting each individual team-strength stat carry over its own separately measured share of last season's value (found to run between 17% and 35%) beats the model's simpler across-the-board setting, which carries over 67% of every stat regardless of what a per-stat estimate would suggest. Tested and resolved: the flat 67% setting wins outright, and letting each stat use its own smaller, separately estimated number actively hurt accuracy.

overlay_single_addition_to_played_union_.classification_evidence: The frozen choice changed ZERO games in the holdout half (interim_hc fires on 5 games across the whole 1,503-game archive and none of them fall in 2023-2025), so the holdout marginal is identically 0.000 with a degenerate interval. That is an uninformative read, not a refutation: no wrong sign is resolved, no reliability is zero, no positive control bounded anything. Category 3. Recorded so the DECISION -- no production change -- rests on a registry entry rather than on prose.
overlay_single_addition_to_played_union_.description: Adding ONE further overlay to the PLAYED four-member union (coach + division_revenge + player_arrests + spread_gap_zone), chosen from ten candidates on opener seasons 2020-2022 ONLY and applied unchanged to 2023-2025. A far smaller selection space than the 4,095-subset re-selection. Frozen choice: interim_hc_first_game_tilt_overlay (+0.142 on the selection half, the only candidate with a positive marginal there).
overlay_single_addition_to_played_union_.notes: Two holdout numbers deliberately NOT acted on because both ranked negative on the selection half, so using them would be selecting on the holdout: pbp08_protection_mismatch_tilt_overlay +1.001 pts week P+ 0.8978 (selection half -0.284), forecast_cold_visitor_tilt +0.501 pts P+ 0.9039 (selection half -0.142). Both remain ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE challengers and 2026 supplies an independent read. Separately measured, as additions to the played union and consistent across BOTH halves: injury_value_lost_tilt_overlay -3.835/-1.252, surface_switch_tilt_overlay -0.284/-1.627 (holdout P+ 0.0220), backup_qb_fade_overlay -0.994/-1.377. That closes nothing about any of them standing alone -- no interval sits wholly on the wrong side of zero on both blockings and no reliability or positive control was run -- it measures only that they subtract as additions to THIS four-member policy on THIS archive.
overlay_single_addition_to_played_union_.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a test of the process for picking a fifth ingredient to add to the four adjustments already layered onto the model's picks (a coach-experience fade, a division-rematch tilt, a player-arrests flip, and a spread-gap fade): a new addition was chosen using only 2020-2022 games, then applied unchanged to the untouched 2023-2025 games to see if the selection process itself holds up going forward. The specific addition chosen this way, a first-year head coach's very first game with that team, produced exactly zero measured difference on the holdout games; two other candidates that looked promising were deliberately not adopted because they only looked good after the fact, and both remain open ideas for future testing.

overlay_stack_combined_opener_2020_2025.classification_evidence: unresolved_below_power, not a terminal closure: the PRIMARY (week-blocked, 107 blocks) interval [-7.478, +1.548] crosses zero (P+ 0.0943 that the combined stack beats the baseline), so wrong_sign_resolved is inadmissible per AGENTS.md ('the wrong sign is a lean, not a resolution' unless the whole interval sits below zero). The season-blocked reading [-6.443, -0.396] (P+ 0.0014) DOES sit entirely below zero, but it is built from only 6 blocks (one per season) and is reported here as a secondary, coarser read, not as grounds for a terminal verdict on its own. No positive control was run. This is also explicitly a diagnostic on already-looked-at windows (several of the six overlays were themselves screened or tuned on spans this archive re-touches), continuous evidence rather than a fresh confirmation, so it would not license a terminal closure even if the primary interval had excluded zero.
overlay_stack_combined_opener_2020_2025.description: Joint (OR-combined: flip if ANY overlay's independent condition fires against the SAME baseline pick) application of all six live pick-flipping ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE overlay challengers atop the active model's own opener-graded picks (production probability rule), 2020-2025, 1537 REG games (1503 non-push, 34 pushes excluded). Baseline accuracy 53.36%, combined-stack accuracy 50.37%. Trigger counts: coach_fade 107, injury_value_lost_tilt 589, division_revenge_tilt 151, backup_qb_fade 181, surface_switch_tilt 239, spread_gap_zone_fade 195 (sum of solo flips 1462, union 1014 games, 365 touched by 2+ overlays). Every overlay's flip equals the complement of the SAME unflipped baseline pick (verified programmatically), so overlap is redundant coverage, never a contradictory recommendation -- zero direction conflicts are possible by construction and zero were found. overlay_stack_combined_opener_2020_2025.plain_summary: This tests what happens if six separate experimental adjustments to the model's picks -- covering a coach-experience fade, an injury-value fade, a division-rematch tilt, a backup-quarterback fade, a playing-surface-switch tilt, and a spread-gap fade -- are all applied together at once, flipping a pick whenever any one of them says to. Combined, these six adjustments actually made the model's picks noticeably worse, dropping accuracy from about 53.4% to about 50.4% across 1,537 games from 2020-2025, and breaking the combination apart shows two of the six (the injury one and the backup-quarterback one) are doing most of the damage on their own.

penalty_crew_high_flag_heavy_underdog_op.plain_summary: Today's officiating crew calls penalties at an unusually high overall rate, and the home team opened as a big underdog, getting at least seven points -- the idea being that the extra stoppages a flag-heavy crew creates help an overmatched home team control tempo and limit possessions against the better team. penalty_crew_holding_tilt_run_heavy.plain_summary: The home team has been run-heavy lately, and today's officiating crew calls offensive holding at an unusually high rate -- the idea being that extra holding scrutiny disrupts a run-blocking scheme more than a passing one, hurting the home team's ability to sustain drives. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of four predeclared officiating-crew-tendency checks, and the limited data actually leaned the other way, toward the home team covering more often in this situation, not less.

penalty_discipline.description: Team penalty rate, quartile split against the market.
penalty_discipline.notes: Re-measured 2026-08-18 via scripts/penalty_discipline_interval.py (this session); no script behind the original 0.67/49.85%/50.52% numbers survives. RECONSTRUCTION: team penalty rate = mean(penalty) over ALL raw REG-season play-by-play rows (no play-type filter) where posteam==team -- of several definitions tried, the only one reproducing the recorded 0.0750 mean / 0.0101 sd / +0.261 year-over-year reliability (this session's independent reproduction: mean 0.07505, sd 0.01013, reliability +0.2604 on 512 team-season pairs -- reconciles ROADMAP's +0.261 phrasing with the registry's stored 0.261, same figure to 3sf). Global quartile split (pd.qcut, 4 bins) of PRIOR-season (lagged) team penalty rate, joined to REG-season team-games (data/processed/game_features.parquet, pushes dropped since home_cover is undefined for them): least-penalized quartile covers 50.56% (n=2069 team-games), most-penalized covers 49.90% (n=2016) -- both within 0.07 points of the recorded 50.52%/49.85%, raw gap +0.655 vs the recorded +0.67 (within the 0.3-point reconstruction tolerance this session was given). Sample: 4,085 team-game rows / 3,070 unique games in the quartile pair (recorded ~4,431, about 8% higher; per-season quartile cuts, including postseason, and scoring pushes as losses were all tried and reproduced the target LESS well, so were rejected in favour of the construction reported here; no surviving script to check the exact discrepancy against, reported not hidden). SCALE (this entry had a scale bug once before, corrected 2026-08-17): the OLD 0.67 effect field was the UNSCALED quartile-pair gap. Following the hc_year_one_fade precedent (raw subset effect x fraction of slate the subset represents), this entry now records the FULL-SLATE-SCALED effect: 0.655 (raw quartile gap, points) x 0.5020 (fraction of the team-game universe the quartile pair represents, since 2 of 4 quartiles are used) = 0.3288 -- THAT is the new effect value; the raw 0.67/0.655 number is preserved here, not silently dropped. UNCERTAINTY: week-blocked (block id = season*100+week, this project's standard convention, 20,000 resamples, seed 20260818, 277 blocks) 95% [-1.0389, +1.6849], se 0.6938, P+ 0.6828 -- RECORDED as this entry's interval/standard_error/probability_positive. Season-blocked secondary (16 season blocks, same seed/samples): 95% [-0.4527, +1.0654], se 0.3887, P+ 0.7886. Both cross zero; per AGENTS.md this is not grounds for rejection, so classification stays unresolved_below_power -- the direction still favours the candidate hypothesis (68-79 percent of resamples, depending on blocking), just not resolvably. sample_blocks (277) is the week-blocked bootstrap's block count under the season*100+week convention, replacing the prior entry's unsourced 17.
penalty_discipline.plain_summary: A team has been among the least penalized in the league over the prior season, compared with the most penalized, checked as a factor in whether that cleaner team covers the spread more often. The limited data leaned toward cleaner teams covering slightly more often, but the underlying numbers here had to be rebuilt from scratch after the original calculation script was lost, so this figure carries extra uncertainty about exactly matching the original measurement.

The family's own predeclaration called a null 'the modal expected outcome, declared acceptable in advance' at this size, so a predicted null cannot close the family. No split-half reliability measured, no positive control. Reclassified closed_negative -> unresolved 2026-08-18.
player_qb_continuity_bundled_alpha.description: QB+lineup continuity features vs base at MISMATCHED regularization (candidate alpha=1, base alpha=10) -- the original, feature-and-alpha-bundled 2014-2017 comparison; distinct from player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.
player_qb_continuity_bundled_alpha.notes: sample_blocks=68 cross-referenced from the sibling matched_alpha entry (same 997-game sample), not independently recomputed for this exact arm pair. DO-NOT-POOL: this entry's effect is algebraically the sum of player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha (+1.1033, feature-only) and the alpha-only contrast (a resolved negative, see REJECTED list) -- recording all three and sign-test-pooling them would triple-count one bit of evidence. See DO-NOT-POOL section below.
player_qb_continuity_bundled_alpha.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this is an old, since-superseded comparison of adding quarterback-and-lineup-continuity features to the model that changed two things in the model at once, both the feature set and a smoothing setting called regularization, making it impossible to tell which change did what. A cleaner comparison elsewhere in this registry changes only the feature set while holding the smoothing setting fixed; this bundled entry adds no new information on its own and is stored here at zero effect for record-keeping only.

player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.classification_evidence: Reclassified 2026-08-18 from refuted_mechanism. The prior refutation stated the two arms 'differ only in ridge alpha (1 vs 10)'; that is factually wrong about THIS entry, whose arms (candidate, base_alpha1) are BOTH alpha=1 and differ only in feature set (measured: predictions.parquet ridge_alpha is 1.0 for both). The near-null-contrast and 0.03%/0.27% shrinkage argument belongs to the SEPARATE alpha-only contrast base_alpha1 vs base_alpha10, which flips only 25/997 picks (2.51%) and is resolvably negative. This feature contrast flips 177/997 (17.75%), split 94-83, paired SE 1.33 pts, MDE80 3.74 pts. The prior evidence also compared a PAIRED delta against an UNPAIRED coin-flip sd (1.58), overstating noise. The two +-1.1033 figures are independent measurements that cancel by algebraic identity (candidate minus base_alpha10 = 0), not one number explaining the other. No split-half reliability was ever measured for the trait and no family-specific positive control exists, so neither admissible closing ground is met.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.description: QB + lineup continuity features, compared at MATCHED regularization (both arms ridge alpha=1); only the feature set differs.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.notes: Window [2014, 2017] remains permanently SPENT; only the interpretation of the spent look changes. sample_blocks switched 4 -> 68: the recorded [0.0, 2.2177] was season-blocked on exactly 4 blocks, on the documented degeneracy floor with a lower bound of exactly 0.0. The 68-week-blocked interval on the identical 997 games is the trustworthy one. Actionable reading unchanged and now better supported: the features want less regularization than the rest of the design, which points at group-wise ridge penalties.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding quarterback-and-lineup-continuity features to the model helps, with the model's smoothing setting held fixed so only the feature set differs between the two versions being compared, on 997 games from the 2014-2017 seasons. The limited data leaned toward the feature block helping; a later re-check found an earlier version of this comparison had used too few time blocks to trust, and the corrected version, on the same games, points the same direction and is now better supported.

proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.classification_evidence: Primary (week-blocked, production probability-rule, pooled 2011-2019 proxy-opener vs 50%) interval [-1.600, +2.370] accuracy points crosses zero with a positive upper bound -- per AGENTS.md this is the EXPECTED shape for a real small signal, not grounds to close. wrong_sign_resolved does not apply (requires the WHOLE interval below zero; this interval's upper bound is positive). No positive-control bound was run, so positive_control_bound does not apply either. The calibration arm's own paired delta (SBR-Open vs true-opener, production rule) is itself unresolved (P+ 0.167, interval crosses zero) so it cannot be used to reclassify this result either. The only admissible classification is unresolved_below_power.
proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.description: Production model (market_residual/weak_stack/ridge alpha=10.0) walked forward week-by-week exactly as nfl_ats.clv.opener_pick_evaluation does, scored with SBR sportsbookreviewsonline.com 'Open' substituted as the settlement/prediction line -- a PROXY for the true Tuesday opener (r=0.949, mean |diff| 1.36-1.37 pts vs the true opener on the only overlap seasons, docs/sbr_odds_archive.md) -- on 11 seasons (2009-2019) the purchased point-in-time market archive cannot reach. 500-game warm-up floor (same constant/mechanism as the rotation registry's rule 9) consumes 2009-2010 entirely; scored population is 2011-2019, 2,304 games, 153 weeks. Reported alongside a same-instrument 2020-2021 dual-grade calibration arm (SBR-Open vs true tue_open, same weekly-refit models, 466 paired games) that measures the proxy discount directly rather than assuming it.
proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.notes: seed=20260817; samples=20000; config=weak_stack/ridge/alpha=10.0 (matches artifacts/active_ats_model.json); min_train_games=500. MAIN ARM: population 2,816/2,816 REG games 2009-2019 have an SBR Open (100% match, 2 flagged open_ambiguous, kept). Warm-up (500-game floor, same mechanism as rotation.py rule 9) consumes 2009-2010 entirely (0 of 34 weeks scorable); 2011-2019 fully scorable. Scored: 2304 games, 153 weeks, seasons 2011-2019. Absolute pooled accuracy: production rule 50.3810%, sign rule 50.4706%. Per-season (sign/production): 2009: warm-up, not scorable; 2010: warm-up, not scorable; 2011: sign 46.80% / prod 45.20%; 2012: sign 50.00% / prod 50.00%; 2013: sign 52.05% / prod 52.46%; 2014: sign 51.78% / prod 51.38%; 2015: sign 49.60% / prod 50.00%; 2016: sign 51.23% / prod 52.87%; 2017: sign 54.03% / prod 52.02%; 2018: sign 49.59% / prod 47.13%; 2019: sign 49.19% / prod 52.42%. Pooled vs 50% coin flip -- PRODUCTION RULE (primary, registered effect is week-blocked): week-blocked estimate=+0.3810 pts, 95% [-1.6001, +2.3702] pts, P+=0.6468; season-blocked estimate=+0.3810 pts, 95% [-1.3671, +1.8652] pts, P+=0.6829. proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.plain_summary: This is an instrument check, not a bet on any game: it estimates how well the prediction model would have performed in the 2011-2019 seasons, for which the project doesn't have real archived opening-line data, by substituting a very similar opening line pulled from a different odds archive as a stand-in. Using that stand-in, the model's accuracy in those older seasons came out around 50.4%, noticeably closer to a coin flip than the roughly 53% to 54% the model achieves in recent seasons with the real opening line, and a companion check on overlapping seasons found only a small, inconclusive part of that gap is explained by the stand-in line differing from the real one -- the rest of the difference is unexplained.

qb_news_backup_visible_by_deadline_scree.description: Backup-QB starts (bias-battery >=3-prior-starts modal-QB construct) foreshadowed by PFT/PFR news headlines (QB full name + injury/start/bench/roster-move keyword, 10-day lookback) before the pool's own per-game deadline (min(kickoff, that week's Sunday 16:00 ET)) -- subset cover rate vs. complement.
qb_news_backup_visible_by_deadline_scree.notes: Revives backup_qb_fade_overlay (killed dead-on-arrival in docs/prospective_evidence.md: schedules.parquet QB-name columns are post-game-only) via timestamped PFT (299,739 urls, docs/injury_news_sourcing.md) + PFR-transactions (72,368 urls, docs/pfr_transactions_sourcing.md) news corpora, per owner correction 2026-08-20 that picks are editable up to each game's own deadline = min(kickoff, that week's Sunday 16:00 ET), not just Tuesday noon. Ground truth: 916 backup starts / 4588 eligible (>=3 prior starts) team-games, 2015-2025, identical construct to bias_battery_backup_qb_start. Visibility (matching rule + buckets frozen in docs/qb_news_channel.md before any cover rate was seen; QB full name + a 64-keyword injury/start/bench/roster-move list, both corpora, 10-day lookback anchored on the deadline): 26.31% by Tuesday noon, 39.96% cumulative by Friday, 44.98% cumulative by Sunday 10am ET-or-deadline (this screen's flag), 47.27% cumulative before the deadline, 52.73% never -- vs. the 2.39%-by-Tuesday-noon comparator for the official Wed-Fri injury report alone (docs/injury_news_sourcing.md sec 5.1), an ~11x improvement from using outlet news instead of the mandated report. Flag = backup start AND news-visible by that bucket; complement = every other eligible team-game. Sign=+1 matches bias_battery_backup_qb_start's own convention exactly (comparable without a flip). Comparators: bias_battery_backup_qb_start -0.2731 pts P+0.1684 (close-graded, 2009-2025, 7002 games); bias_battery_backup_qb_start_opener -2.3578 pts P+0.0982 (opener-graded, 2020-2025, 2436 games). This news-visible subset leans the SAME (negative) direction but is MUCH weaker (P+0.39145 vs 0.098-0.168) than the full backup-start population -- my inference, not measured: foreshadowed backups may already be partly priced by the time other bettors see the same news, unlike silent backup starts; not verified here. SNF/MNF deadline correction (owner, 2026-08-20): 313/916 backup-start games had kickoff after that week's Sunday 16:00 ET (258 late-Sunday/SNF, 55 Monday) and were therefore potentially affected; directly measured only 3/916 (0.33%) had their earliest qualifying match actually fall in the [Sunday 16:00 ET, kickoff) gap under a plain-kickoff boundary, so the correction is real but immaterial to the headline number -- applied and re-run anyway (this entry's numbers are the corrected-deadline run, not the plain-kickoff run). Reliability: not_applicable -- like backup_qb_start itself, this is a per-game situational flag (this start's own news timing), not a persistent per-team/per-entity trait; nothing to split-half. Week-blocked (block=season*100+week), 20000 resamples, seed=20260819, full-slate scaling (fraction_of_slate=0.0898) per scripts/nfl_bias_battery_screen.py convention. No rotation-registry window drawn (screen precedent, not a spec-registered family). EV note: another agent is wiring the late-week refresh pipeline; nothing here is wired into any live pick path -- this is measurement only.
qb_news_backup_visible_by_deadline_scree.plain_summary: A team is starting a backup quarterback, restricted to the cases where sports-news outlets had already reported the backup would likely start before the pick deadline, rather than it coming as a surprise. Teams starting a backup quarterback generally cover less often overall, but this narrower slice, where the change was foreshadowed in the news, leaned the same losing direction only weakly, suggesting the betting market may already price in backup-quarterback news reported in advance, unlike a truly surprise change; that explanation is inferred here, not directly proven.

recurrence_flags_player_brier_validation.notes: COHERENCE FIX 2026-08-26, two defects in one row. (2) It violated the storage convention at src/nfl_ats/weak_signals.py line 112: effects are stored so POSITIVE FAVOURS THE CANDIDATE whatever the metric polarity, and brier improves downward, so a worse-than-baseline brier delta must be stored NEGATED. Raw test-2024 delta is +0.0433 (line 100) and has NO bootstrap interval anywhere in artifacts/recurrence_hazard/validation_metrics.json; a test row would need its own paired bootstrap. Apparent gain vs RAW base was pure recalibration. Same-history hazard ratios echo published RRs directionally (hamstring 2.01, shoulder 1.95 vs published 2.7). recurrence_flags_player_brier_validation.plain_summary: Not a bet on games directly: this measures whether tracking a player's history of repeat injuries to the same body part improves the model's forecast of whether that player will be available for next week's game, scored on a probability-accuracy scale (Brier score) rather than the usual pick-accuracy percentage, using 2022 data to build the method and 2023 games held out to check it. This entry had two bookkeeping errors caught and fixed in the same update, a wrong interval paired with the number and a flipped plus/minus sign; corrected, the recurrence-history information only beats an already-outdated, uncalibrated baseline, and the apparent gain disappears once that baseline is properly calibrated.

redteam_body_clock_night_increment_withi.description: Red-team specificity split: LPM of home_cover on night kickoff (>=20:00 ET) + distance among WEST-body-clock road teams only (day+night), week-clustered SEs; coefficient on the night flag
redteam_body_clock_night_increment_withi.notes: WARNING for claim-3 consumers: the dose decomposition between 'west road' and 'night' is not separately established; matched >=807mi night-vs-day gap is -3.39 pts. Correlated with body_clock_* family; never pool as independent.
redteam_body_clock_night_increment_withi.plain_summary: This is a stress-test of the West Coast body-clock travel effect: among West Coast teams playing a road game at night (8pm ET kickoff or later), it isolates the effect of the late kickoff time itself while holding travel distance constant. It leaned toward hurting those teams' covering rate, but the notes are explicit that this check alone cannot cleanly separate how much of the effect is the late kickoff versus the travel distance, and it should not be treated as independent evidence alongside the related body-clock entries it decomposes.

redteam_body_clock_night_west_road_dista.classification_evidence: Attack FAILED to kill the parent: west-night gap survives holding travel distance constant (z=-2.17), distance coefficient has the wrong sign to confound; whole interval on claimed side but no terminal classification is warranted for a supporting control
redteam_body_clock_night_west_road_dista.description: Red-team distance control for body_clock_night_west_road_ge2000et: LPM of home_cover on west-body-clock visitor + haversine travel distance (per 1000mi) among night (>=20:00 ET) road games, week-clustered SEs; coefficient on the west flag
redteam_body_clock_night_west_road_dista.notes: Answers 'is west-road-at-night just long-distance road': NO at this resolution. Correlated with body_clock_night_west_road_ge2000et; never pool as independent. Normal-approximation P+ from clustered LPM, not block bootstrap.
redteam_body_clock_night_west_road_dista.plain_summary: This is a follow-up check on the West Coast body-clock travel effect: it asks whether a West Coast team's road game at night really comes down to sheer travel distance, by testing for an effect specifically tied to being a West Coast team even after accounting for how far it traveled. The answer leaned clearly toward no, the effect held up even after controlling for distance, but this uses a quicker statistical shortcut than the project's usual method and is explicitly flagged as not independent evidence from the related body-clock entries it decomposes.

redteam_bye_fade_sham_placebo_null.classification_evidence: Placebo-validation cell, not a tradable signal: observed real-assignment effect +0.5508 exceeds 99% of sham draws (P(placebo >= observed)=0.01), so the placebo FAILED to kill the mechanism; recording the null distribution itself, classified unresolved_below_power because no registry class fits an instrument-validation cell
redteam_bye_fade_sham_placebo_null.description: SHAM-bye placebo for the bye fade: 100 draws shifting every team's true strict-bye +/-2 weeks within its season, fade-full-slate cell rebuilt identically; distribution of draw-level effects
redteam_bye_fade_sham_placebo_null.notes: NEVER POOL - validation cell only. Sham mean -0.2083, sd 0.3144, q97.5 +0.4434. Supports bye_overval_fade_full_slate_post2011's mechanism reading.
redteam_bye_fade_sham_placebo_null.plain_summary: Placebo: this fakes each team's bye week by randomly shifting it one or two weeks off from where it actually fell, then reruns the exact same 'fade the team coming off a bye' bet on those fictional bye weeks, repeated 100 times. Since the bye weeks used here aren't real, any effect this finds is noise the method invents on its own; it came back close to zero, which supports treating the real bye-week finding elsewhere in this registry as a genuine pattern rather than an artifact of the method.

redteam_bye_overval_fade_full_slate_with.classification_evidence: Reproduction/stability cell for the parent signal under a corrected instrument; near-duplicate of bye_overval_fade_full_slate_post2011 (P+ 0.870 vs 0.834), no terminal ground applies

redteam_bye_overval_fade_full_slate_with.notes: Correlated with bye_overval_fade_full_slate_post2011 - never pool as independent. Bootstrap 4000 samples, seed 20260863.
redteam_bye_overval_fade_full_slate_with.plain_summary: A team is coming off its bye week. This re-tests the bet against that team using a corrected way of identifying bye weeks that avoids a bug which had been mislabeling every season-opening game as coming off a bye. The limited data leaned toward the bet working, and this result is a bug-fixed re-run of an existing bye-week finding elsewhere in this registry rather than independent new evidence.

This is the depth-players-only half of that check, and the limited data leaned only weakly and inconclusively toward hurting that team, unlike the starters-only half, which is a stronger, separate finding elsewhere in this registry.

redteam_nflcom_out2_starters_only.plain_summary: A team has at least two players officially listed as Out for Friday's injury report, and at least two of them are regular starters who played at least half their team's snaps the week before, a decomposition built to check whether an existing 'multiple players Out' finding is really about losing starters rather than just losing bodies. It leaned very strongly toward hurting that team's chances, confirming that losing starters, not just roster depth, drives the underlying finding, though this is itself a decomposition of that existing finding rather than independent new evidence.

redteam_overlay_subset_loso_cv.notes: WARNING: damages the '~+1pt fair expectation' framing - best direct estimate is a coin flip (P+ 0.493). Correlated with overlay_subset_* entries; never pool as independent. Week-blocked bootstrap seed 20260836.
redteam_overlay_subset_loso_cv.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this is a robustness check on how the model chooses which combination of overlay adjustments to use, by picking the best-looking combination from five seasons of data and then testing that fixed choice on a sixth season it never saw, repeated one held-out season at a time. The result came back essentially a coin flip, which undercuts an earlier, more optimistic expectation for how much this piece of the model should be worth.

residual_location_train_recency_hl100_cf.plain_summary: College football: this is a model-settings test, not a bet on any game -- it checks whether weighting the games used to originally train the model's scoring formula more heavily toward recent games, fading out over roughly 100 games, beats training on all past games equally, isolating that idea from a related, already-tested one about weighting errors after training rather than the training data itself.
