ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation.classification_evidence:
PRIMARY (opener grade, n=1,537 paired games, 107 weeks, 2020-2025): baseline 52.83% vs candidate 51.43%, paired candidate-minus-baseline delta -1.397 pts, week-blocked 95% CI [-3.15, +0.27] pts, P+ 0.0504; season-blocked 95% CI [-2.69, +0.26] pts, P+ 0.0429. The upper bound of both intervals still crosses zero, so per AGENTS.md's binding rule this stays unresolved (category-3), not refuted, despite a ~95-96% lean against the candidate.
SECONDARY (close grade, same paired games; per AGENTS.md this may never veto the opener-graded primary and did not need to): delta -0.332 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.350, season-blocked P+ 0.294 -- same direction, much weaker, closer to genuinely unresolved.
CALIBRATION DIRECTION (Brier/log-loss, same opener-graded paired games): improves in the candidate's favor, P+ 0.77-0.90 across week/season blocking (Brier P+ 0.771 week / 0.862 season; log-loss P+ 0.802 week / 0.895 season). On the separate nflverse_spread full-history grade (2,075 games, 2018-2025) this direction resolves outright at season-blocking: Brier P+ 0.9995, log-loss P+ 1.000.
MULTIPLICITY: alpha=2,000 was pre-localized on the CFB instrument by two predeclared grids (13-point coarse log-grid 1e-3-1e5, then a 6-point refinement after the coarse Brier curve turned over near 1,000-3,000), both already recorded in docs/ridge_alpha.md and the ridge_alpha_global registry entry. This NFL run is one confirmation look at that already-localized value on a different instrument, not a search -- no alpha grid was swept here, no alternative candidate was tried.
CROSS-INSTRUMENT SIGN DISAGREEMENT: CFB's own accuracy screen at this alpha leans positive for the candidate (+0.258 pts, P+ 0.756 week / 0.711 season, docs/ridge_alpha.md), while this NFL opener-graded look leans negative (P+ 0.04-0.05) and the NFL nflverse-graded look also leans negative but less decisively (P+ 0.16-0.23). The two instruments disagree on accuracy's sign while agreeing on Brier/log-loss's sign -- consistent with docs/ridge_alpha.md sec2b's reading that the accuracy curve's apparent bumps are noise scatter around a genuinely flat surface rather than a real effect.
ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation.description: Confirmation swap of the active production model's ridge_alpha from the frozen incumbent (10.0) to the CFB-localized candidate docs/ridge_alpha.md sec4 names for exactly this scenario (2,000.0) -- weak_stack/market_residual/ridge, calibration=none, every other setting held fixed. Opener-graded (pool-relevant), paired same-games comparison on the full 2020-2025 archive.
ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation.notes: Reviewer adjudication 2026-08-18: production swap REFUSED on EV -- the same rule that promoted MOD-07 at 87/13 reads this as ~95/5 AGAINST at the opener grade. alpha=10 remains underived but now holds a measured opener-graded defense against the nominated alternative. The resolved calibration gain routes to Best-Pick/calibration consumers, not to the accuracy-graded production model. Baseline arm reproduced docs/opener_evaluation.md's 52.83%/51.56% and active_ats_model.json's 51.566% exactly before the comparison was trusted. DO-NOT-POOL: opener-graded promotion comparison on the paired opener population, different grade/population from most NFL entries.
ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation.plain_summary: Not a bet on any game: this tests swapping one of the live model's own settings -- the dial that controls how heavily it smooths noise out of its inputs -- from its current value of 10 up to 2,000, a setting that had worked better in college football testing, then checks the swap head-to-head against the current setting on the real NFL opening-line record. The swap was tested and rejected: at the openers the project actually plays, the higher setting looked about 19-to-1 likely to be worse, not better, so the model kept its original setting.

ridge_alpha_global.classification_evidence: Week-blocked interval contains zero (P+ 0.758); season-blocked P+ 0.703, also unresolved. This is a SECOND LOOK: alpha=2,500 was chosen after a coarse 13-point predeclared grid (1e-3..1e5) showed the Brier curve turning over near 1,000-3,000, then a 6-point refinement grid localized the minimum. The refinement narrows a point estimate; it does not license a stronger claim than the coarse grid already supports (coarse alpha=3,000: accuracy +0.213 pts, P+ 0.716/0.659; Brier +0.000294, P+ 0.933/0.894). The Brier half IS resolved and consistent across the whole 300-10,000 band (all P+ >= 0.75, most >= 0.93), which is the resolvable companion result -- see notes.
ridge_alpha_global.description: Global ridge penalty (market_residual / weak_stack, CFB walk-forward screen, 2,000-alpha grid) vs the frozen production alpha=10. Brier/log-loss improve with high confidence in a broad 300-10,000 band (peak near 2,000-2,500); forced-pick accuracy does not move.
ridge_alpha_global.notes: Blocked behind: the active production model runs alpha=10, which shrinks the median principal direction of the fitted design by only 0.27% (docs/ridge_alpha.md sec 1) -- i.e. alpha does essentially nothing on the ~70 well-conditioned, signal-bearing directions and is not chosen with any bias-variance tradeoff in mind. Accuracy is flat across [0.001, 10000], a 7-order-of-magnitude range, with no candidate clearing P+ >= 0.90 on both week- and season-blocking. Route the Brier gain to the Best Pick ranker (docs/pool_edge_plan.md queue item 2), not to a production accuracy swap. Do not pool this with groupwise_ridge_block_penalties without checking commensurability -- different mechanism (global penalty level vs. per-block allocation), though both are ridge-penalty-structure findings on the same CFB instrument with the same accuracy/Brier split pattern.
ridge_alpha_global.plain_summary: College football: this tests turning up the same model-smoothing dial (from 10 to a wide range including 2,000-2,500) using only the free college football data. A much higher setting made the model's own confidence levels noticeably more trustworthy on that data, but did not change how many picks the model actually got right, so the finding was routed toward whichever part of the system relies on trustworthy confidence numbers (like ranking picks by how sure the model is) rather than toward the accuracy setting itself.

Raw gap leans negative (closed-when-benign covers 44.83% vs complement 50.25%, P+=0.0870 for a POSITIVE gap under the fixed +1 sign, i.e. most draws are negative) but no direction was predeclared for this cell, so this is reported as an exploratory lean, not a confirmed or refuted hypothesis. No refuted mechanism, no positive-control bound.
roof_battery_closed_benign_forecast_vs_o.description: Exploratory, NO predeclared direction (sign fixed at +1, raw gap as-is). Subset=roof CLOSED despite a benign pregame NDFD/GFS-MOS forecast (>=50F, <=15mph wind, both thresholds fixed before scoring) -- a 'comfort'/revealed-preference closure, not a weather-necessitated one; complement=everyone else in the league. 2020-2025 only (forecast_archive coverage gate). Home team's own ATS cover rate. Mined cell (4 of 5 predeclared, the only one with no directional hypothesis), uncorrected multiplicity.
roof_battery_closed_benign_forecast_vs_o.notes: schedules.parquet's own temp/wind fields are ~100% NaN for every retractable-venue game regardless of roof state (measured) -- the only local source with an independent pregame forecast at the stadium's own coordinates is data/raw/forecast_archive/full_2020_2025/forecasts.parquet (NDFD/GFS-MOS, 100% populated for both open/closed retractable games in that table). n_flag=145 closed-and-benign games out of 3,164 team-game rows in the 2020-2025 window. Side count (anecdotal, NOT bootstrapped, too rare to test): 9 games where roof was OPEN despite a non-benign forecast. Operational timing: the benign/non-benign FORECAST classification is itself Tuesday-safe (NDFD/GFS-MOS forecasts are available days ahead), but the cell as a whole is still gated on the actual roof OUTCOME, which is only known ~T-90min before kickoff (footballzebras.com policy explainer) -- so this cell stays kickoff-adjacent overall, playable via the refresh pass, NOT usable at the Tuesday lock, despite the Tuesday-safe weather half.
roof_battery_closed_benign_forecast_vs_o.plain_summary: A team plays at a stadium with a retractable roof and chooses to keep it CLOSED even though the forecast that day was mild (50F or warmer, wind under 15 mph) -- a 'didn't need to close it' situation rather than a weather-forced one. This was tested, with no direction guessed in advance, as one of five checks in a roof-decision batch, and the limited data (145 qualifying games) leaned toward the home team covering less often in that spot -- though the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed.description: Home team's own ATS cover rate at a retractable-roof venue: subset=roof OPEN vs complement=everyone else in the league. Mechanism: open roof strips these 5 franchises' climate-controlled home identity, hypothesized to hurt HOME cover. Mined cell (1 of 5 predeclared), uncorrected multiplicity.
roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed.notes: Retractable population (measured, data-driven): home_team in {ARI,ATL,DAL,HOU,IND} AND roof in {open,closed}, n=626 REG games 2009-2025 before push-dropping. ATL restricted to its Mercedes-Benz Stadium era (2017+) automatically since pre-2017 Georgia Dome games are tagged 'dome', not open/closed. LV/LA/LAC (SoFi) are fixed-roof domes in nflverse's own schema, treated as controls, not retractable. Three 2020 SF home games relocated to State Farm Stadium (COVID) are excluded since home_team=SF is not in the retractable set. n_flag=81 open-roof team-games (of 84 raw open games, 3 pushes dropped). Era split (2009-2016 vs 2017-2025 boundary = ATL's Mercedes-Benz Stadium entering the retractable set): subset_cover is 4/9=0.4444 in BOTH eras independently (16/36 and 20/45 -- verified per-season, a real small-integer coincidence, not a bug); full_slate_effect +0.0506pts (P+=0.7225, n_flag=36) 2009-2016 vs +0.0543pts (P+=0.7490, n_flag=45) 2017-2025 -- consistent direction and similar magnitude across both eras, not a case of a weak-era reading masking absence. Operational timing: BACKTEST cell, roof tag read post-hoc from the completed game record (no leakage in the measurement). Live roof status is announced ~90min before kickoff (footballzebras.com policy explainer, cited docs/data_source_scout_v4.md rank #6) -- after this project's Tuesday line freeze but before kickoff. Per project memory (picks editable to kickoff, only lines freeze Tuesday), this is a legitimate KICKOFF-ADJACENT refresh-pass input, NOT usable at the Tuesday lock. No live T-90 scrape pipeline exists in this repo yet. Re-screened at OPENER grade as roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed_opener (2020-2025 archive intersection, sign flips to P+=0.2736 -- reported separately, not averaged in.
roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed.plain_summary: At one of the five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof, the roof is OPEN for today's game rather than closed, stripping that team of its usual climate-controlled home-field identity. vi_disp_homecover_top_vs_bottom_tercile.plain_summary: Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the spread on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday betting boards -- among the top third of most-disagreed-upon games -- compared with games in the bottom third, where the books are unusually close together. Bet on the home team, using only 2009-2016 seasons, and the limited data leaned fairly strongly toward the idea, though this is a second, related look at a family of checks built on the very same stretch of games as several other entries in this registry, so it should not be treated as independent confirmation of them.

vi_disp_movement_top_vs_bottom_tercile.plain_summary: This one measures how much the final betting line moved from open to close, in points, not whether a pick was right, so it answers a different question on a different scale than most entries here. Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the spread on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday boards -- the idea being that more early disagreement should mean more repricing by kickoff -- compared with games where the books agree closely. The limited 2009-2016 data leaned slightly the other way, toward less line movement in the high-disagreement games, not more, and one single early season in the data is a likely outlier skewing this read.

It does show a strong lean toward the underdog in the data, which matters for reading a related 'high disagreement' finding elsewhere in this registry: the two are correlated results from the same pool of games and should not be added together as if independent.

vi_totaldisp_overshoot_top_vs_bottom_ter.plain_summary: This one is about the total-points (over/under) market, not which team wins against the spread, and it's measured in points of overshoot past the total line, not pick accuracy, so it answers a different question on a different scale. Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the total-points line on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday boards -- among the top third of most-disagreed-upon games -- compared with the bottom third. Both groups of games finished under their opening total on average, and the high-disagreement group undershot by even more than the low-disagreement group, the opposite of what was expected, though the underlying idea for which direction to expect was only weakly grounded to begin with.

weak_stack_v3_nfl_opener_confirmation.classification_evidence: PRIMARY (opener grade, production probability rule, n=1,537 paired games, 107 weeks, 2020-2025): baseline 53.36% vs candidate 53.03%, paired candidate-minus-baseline delta -0.333 pts, week-blocked 95% CI [-2.107, +1.467] pts, P+ 0.3415; season-blocked (6 season blocks -- below MIN_BLOCKS_FOR_INTERVAL=10, degenerate, reported for completeness only) delta -0.333 pts, CI [-1.596, +0.915] pts, P+ 0.2966. Both intervals cross zero, so per AGENTS.md's binding rule this stays unresolved_below_power (category 3), not refuted -- the naive week-blocked interval does not even sit entirely below zero, so no widening-factor check is needed to rule out wrong_sign_resolved. EV read at the opener (primary, pool-relevant grade): P+ 0.3415 for the candidate, i.e. roughly 2-to-1 the incumbent weak_stack is better here, not strong enough to promote and not strong enough to refute the gap features either.
weak_stack_v3_nfl_opener_confirmation.description: weak_stack_v3 candidate profile (active weak_stack plus every buildable NFL registry gap feature with probability_positive >= 0.60: division revenge, sandwich spot, post-blowout letdown/bounce, penalty rate, surface switch, thursday-pure, return-trip hangover -- 15 new columns) vs the active production weak_stack, opener grade primary (production probability rule, home_cover_probability>=0.5), paired 2020-2025 Tuesday-opener archive, both arms ridge_alpha=10.0/regressor=ridge/target=market_residual held fixed so the delta isolates the 15 gap columns.
weak_stack_v3_nfl_opener_confirmation.notes:
SECONDARY (opener grade, historical sign rule residual_at_open>0, same paired games; per AGENTS.md may never veto the primary and did not need to): delta -0.732 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.211, season-blocked P+ 0.279 -- same direction, somewhat stronger lean against.
SECONDARY (close grade, same paired games; per AGENTS.md a close-graded number may never veto the opener-graded primary): probability rule delta +0.332 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.619, season-blocked P+ 0.586; sign rule delta +0.133 pts, week-blocked P+ 0.545. Direction flips vs the opener (mildly favours the candidate at close) -- the two grades disagree, exactly the situation AGENTS.md's opener-grading rule exists to adjudicate; the primary verdict above is the opener number.
CALIBRATION DIRECTION (Brier/log-loss, opener-graded paired games): both lean AGAINST the candidate -- Brier P+ 0.193 week / 0.246 season, log-loss P+ 0.181 week / 0.230 season. Consistent with the accuracy lean, not contradicting it.
PICK FLIPS: 189 of 1537 games (12.3%) disagree under the production probability rule, 207 (13.5%) under the sign rule -- the 15 gap columns move a substantial share of picks, not a token amount.
COMPOSITION: weak_stack_v3 = weak_stack_surface (weak_stack + surface_switch_flag, itself registry entry surface_switch_feature_arm P+ 0.6181) plus 3 new sub-families built this session in src/nfl_ats/weak_stack_v3_features.py -- gap_v3_bias (division revenge/sandwich spot/post-blowout letdown+bounce, 12 columns, ported from nfl_ats.experiment_runner.FLAG_BUILDERS and scripts/nfl_bias_battery_screen.py), gap_v3_penalty (diff_penalty_rate_prior, ported from scripts/weak_stack_v2_eval.py, already registry entry weak_stack_v2_penalty_only P+ 0.6939), gap_v3_travel (thursday-pure + return-trip hangover, ported from scripts/nfl_travel_rest_battery_screen.py). This is a POOLED candidate, not a single mechanism -- its combined-arm result does not individually confirm or refute any one input family; each input keeps its own existing registry entry and classification.
Baseline arm reproduced docs/opener_evaluation.md's 53.36% production-rule opener headline and artifacts/active_ats_model.json's tracked figure before the comparison was trusted (measured this session).
DO-NOT-POOL: opener-graded profile-vs-profile promotion comparison on the paired opener population; correlated with every other opener-graded weak_stack-baseline entry (ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation, surface_switch_feature_arm's own inputs, etc) through the shared baseline arm and shared 1,537-game population.
weak_stack_v3_nfl_opener_confirmation.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this bundles fifteen separate situational inputs together -- things like division-rivalry revenge games, a team sandwiched between two tough opponents, letdowns or bounce-backs after a blowout, penalty rates, playing-surface switches, short-week Thursday games, and long-trip travel hangovers -- and adds all fifteen to the production model at once, tested at the project's most rigorous opening-line grading standard on 1,537 games across six seasons. As a combined bundle it leaned against helping, and a meaningful 12 to 14 percent of picks flipped compared with the current model, though each of the fifteen inputs keeps its own separate finding elsewhere in this registry and this bundled result doesn't confirm or rule out any one of them individually.

It nonetheless leans hard against the candidate (P+ 0.0956 week-blocked, 0.1629 season-blocked), which is what decides the PLAY on expected value: keeping the incumbent is the ~90/10 favoured side. Both arms hold ridge_alpha=10.0 and regressor=ridge fixed; only feature_profile differs. Baseline 53.36% (matches the tracked production figure exactly), candidate 52.30%, on 1,537 paired Tuesday-opener games over 107 weeks / 2020-2025. Predeclared in docs/weak_stack_v4.md before scoring.
weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_pr.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this adds six raw pregame weather-forecast numbers (temperature, wind, and similar readings from the forecast closest to kickoff) directly into the production model, tested at the project's most rigorous opening-line grading standard on 1,537 games across six seasons. Accuracy dropped from 53.36% for the current model to 52.30% with the forecast columns added, a lean against adopting this specific way of using forecast weather.

weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.classification_evidence: The ENTIRE week-blocked interval [-3.3467, -0.5940] sits below zero, and the season-blocked interval [-3.2720, -0.8291] does too, with P+ 0.00255 and 0.0 respectively. That is a RESOLVED wrong sign on this endpoint -- the admissible closing ground wrong_sign_resolved -- not an interval-contains-zero rejection. Paired Brier and log-loss at the opener agree and also exclude zero (-0.001574 [-0.002839, -0.000336] P+ 0.0064; -0.003192 [-0.005787, -0.000648] P+ 0.0071), so the probability quality moved the same way as the picks. Scope of this closure is EXACTLY this construction: six continuous forecast columns added to a ~275-column ridge at alpha=10 under the sign rule. It closes nothing about forecast weather as a phenomenon -- see notes.
weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.description: Same run and same paired 1,537-game population as weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_probability_rule, scored under the predeclared SIGN rule (residual_at_open > 0) rather than the production probability rule. Baseline 52.83%, candidate 50.90%. Reported for comparability with prior opener-grade runs; the probability rule is the primary endpoint per docs/opener_evaluation.md.
weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.notes: Does NOT touch the registered pick-level forecast cells. forecast_weather_kn_warm_team_cold_late_full (+0.1686 accuracy points, week-blocked [+0.0091, +0.3169], P+ 0.9800) and its siblings are a different construction -- a narrow post-prediction pick-level tilt on ~1.5% of the slate -- and remain live as prospective challengers. This arm tested whether ridge extracts MORE from the raw continuous variables than those hand-coded cells do; it does not, on this population. Inferred mechanism, not measured: the market prices the same public forecast, so the columns mostly add variance to a market-residual model that is already near-sufficient, consistent with this project's own team-quality-is-already-priced finding. 142 picks flipped under the probability rule and the baseline was right on 55.8% of them versus the candidate's 44.2%, so the flips were actively harmful rather than neutral.
weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.plain_summary: This tests one way of feeding pregame weather forecasts into the prediction model: adding six raw forecast numbers into the model's large regression, then picking a side only by whether the market's own weather-adjusted line and the raw forecast disagree in direction, instead of using the model's usual probability output. Tested head to head against the production approach on the same 1,537 opening-line games, this version dragged accuracy down from 52.83% to 50.90%, a resolved loss rather than an inconclusive result. A separate, narrower way of using forecast weather -- applied after picks are already made, not built into the regression -- is a different construction and remains a live idea, unaffected by this result.

weather_battery_dome_team_outdoors_cold.notes: Battery multiplicity: one of 8 predeclared cells in the NFL weather/environment bias battery (scripts/nfl_weather_battery_screen.py), scored on the same 4,317-row REG 2009-2025 population (114 pushes/rows with missing result or spread_line dropped from 4,431 REG games); mined/exploratory; do not sign-test-pool battery cells as independent. All 8 cells share seed 20260819, 20000 bootstrap draws. n_missing_required_data=1390 rows had a required wind/temp input missing -- flag forced False, included in complement. Measured breakdown of the 1390: 1192 are dome/closed-roof games where wind/temp is structurally not applicable indoors (not a data gap), and 199 are genuinely missing outdoor-game observations, concentrated in 2009-2019 (roughly 1-6%/season) with a data-quality spike in 2022 (49% of outdoor games missing wind/temp that season) and 2023 (22%) -- notably not just the pre-2016 pattern anticipated going in. Season-blocked secondary bootstrap (block=season, n=17 seasons): 95% [-0.1031, +0.3288] P+=0.832 (robustness check, not the registry interval).

weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.classification_evidence: Recorded category 3 DESPITE being a control arm, because the strict AGENTS.md ground is 'bounded by a positive control PROVEN ABLE to detect an effect that size', and this run proves no such detection capability -- it shows an absence, which is not the same thing. The week-blocked interval [-2.8170, +0.4610] contains zero, so no wrong sign is resolved either. What IS measured, and what makes this decision-relevant: the oracle arm (-1.131 pts) and the real-forecast arm weak_stack_v4 (-1.065 pts) are statistically indistinguishable, so the ORACLE-MINUS-FORECAST GAP is -0.066 accuracy points. That gap is the entire headroom available to better weather forecasting on this path, and it is approximately zero and slightly negative. Reliability is not_applicable: this is a whole-profile comparison, not a per-team trait with a year-over-year value to split-half.
weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.description: POSITIVE-CONTROL arm: production weak_stack plus the weather that ACTUALLY happened (observed temp/wind, a forecast of infinite skill), vs the active weak_stack profile at the OPENER grade under the production probability rule. Deliberately leaky and never promotable; it exists to bound what ANY improvement in weather forecasting could be worth. Both arms hold ridge_alpha=10.0 and regressor=ridge fixed, on the same 1,537 paired Tuesday-opener games over 2020-2025, so the only difference from the weak_stack_v4 forecast arm is forecast skill. Baseline 53.3599%, oracle 52.2289%. Predeclared in docs/weak_stack_v4.md before scoring.
weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.notes: Answers the owner hypothesis that the forecast arm failed because forecasting is not accurate enough. Measured, that is not the explanation: the kickoff-nearest archive has a median 6.0-hour lead time and temperature r=0.964 / MAE 3.25F against the observed value, and this arm shows that even PERFECT weather does not help. Wind is the leg where the hypothesis had teeth (r=0.649, MAE 3.16 mph at that same lead), and the oracle covers wind too -- so a better wind source has a measured ceiling of about -0.07 points on this construction. Scope: this is the FEATURE-vector construction only. It says nothing about the pick-level weather CELLS, which are a different construction on ~1.5% of the slate and remain ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE challengers (forecast_weather_kn_warm_team_cold_late at P+ 0.9800, forecast_weather_kn_precip_high_total, forecast_cold_visitor_tilt). Coverage caveat: observed weather exists for 3,010 of 4,902 rows (61.4%) -- indoor games and unmapped stations have none -- so this is an oracle over the games that have an observation, with nulls imputed on the training fold like every other family.
weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.plain_summary: Not a bet, and not something anyone could ever actually have before kickoff: this control test hands the model the weather that truly occurred on gameday, as if the forecast were perfect, to measure the absolute most that better weather forecasting could ever be worth to the production model. Even perfect information made accuracy worse, not better (53.36% fell to 52.23%), which rules out 'the forecast just isn't accurate enough' as the reason an earlier weather-forecast test underperformed; for wind specifically, the same method puts the ceiling on a better wind source at only about -0.07 points, essentially nothing. This result only concerns feeding raw weather into the model's core regression -- it says nothing about a handful of separate, narrower weather-based picks elsewhere in this registry that remain live possibilities.
